subject: Request: withdrawal option + capped per-incident liability for uptime breaches
messages:
From: Emma Cho <emma.cho@olivetech.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@olivetech.com
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up on SLA: request for withdrawal option + capped per-incident liability

Alex —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. As we prep our internal approval packet, Procurement and Legal asked us to put a concrete ask on the table so we can model our risk. Two items they want included in the SOW/Order Form: 

1) A "withdrawal option" that allows us to terminate for repeated severity-2 outages (e.g., more than 5 sev-2/hour over a rolling 30-day window) with 30 days' notice and pro-rated refund of pre-paid committed fees. This is to align with our operational risk profile.

2) A capped per-incident monetary liability (not just service credits) for outages that materially impact latency/throughput where credits won't make us whole. Suggested approach: capped at 20% of monthly committed spend per incident, with an overall annual cap of 100% of annual committed spend.

I appreciate this is beyond Redwood's standard credit-only posture, but Olivetech is onboarding customer-facing features in Q1 and needs a strong remedy if things fail. Please let us know what is feasible; if needed we'll have Legal jump on a quick call.

Attachments: Olivetech_SLA_request_20261129.pdf (annotated asks)

—Emma

Subject: Fwd: Olivetech SLA asks — need quick legal/ops sanity check

Folks — forwarding Olivetech's asks (attached). Key points: they want a 30-day withdrawal option triggered by repeated sev-2s and an option to claim per-incident monetary liability (proposed 20% monthly commit per incident; annual cap = 100% annual commit).

Questions I have for Legal/Prod: 
- Is there an acceptable template for a time-boxed "withdrawal" clause limited to Dedicated/Private customers only? We should avoid open-ended termination exposure for hosted multitenant. 
- Can we offer a capped buyout instead of per-incident damages — e.g., Olivetech can buy out the remaining term at a fixed multiplier of remaining committed fees if the withdrawal condition is met? That keeps us away from open damages. 
- If we consider per-incident cash remedies, what's the maximum per-incident exposure Legal is comfortable with while protecting company indemnity and reinsurance?

Attaching Olivetech PDF and our MAP. Quick replies welcome — Emma is tracking approvals week of Dec 6.

—Alex
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T08:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Olivetech SLA asks — need quick legal/ops sanity check

Alex / team —

Thanks for escalating. High level legal view below (quick notes, not final redlines):

1) Withdrawal option: We can agree to a narrowly scoped withdrawal right but must instrument it as a contractual "buyout" rather than a one-way termination for convenience. Proposal: if withdrawal trigger occurs (defined carefully by severity thresholds and confirmed incident post-mortems), Olivetech may elect to exit the committed term by paying a buyout equal to 3 months of committed fees or the pro-rated remainder of the term, whichever is lower. This avoids indefinite refunds and protects our revenue predictability. Limit to Dedicated/Private deployments only; exclude hosted multitenant unless Legal signs off separately.

2) Per-incident monetary liability: We do not want open-ended liquidated damages. Acceptable compromise: a discrete per-incident buyout pool capped at 10% of monthly committed spend per incident, with an annual aggregate cap of 50% of annual committed spend. In lieu of cash, we can offer expedited service-level credits plus priority remediation credits and a one-time invoice credit equal to the buyout cap for the incident. Rationale: keeps exposure bounded and aligns with insurability.

3) Operational guardrails: require RCA within 10 business days, require joint verification of severity metrics, and exclude incidents caused by customer-managed components or force majeure.

If Sales/RevOps are comfortable with these numbers, I can draft specific language and limited SOW amendment. 

—Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up on SLA: request for withdrawal option + capped per-incident liability

Alex —

Appreciate the quick internal review and Monica's proposals. Olivetech can accept a buyout mechanism rather than an unconditional refund, but two asks before we proceed to Legal review: 

1) Can you increase the per-incident cap to 15% of monthly committed spend? Our SRE team says 10% would not sufficiently cover remediation and third-party passthrough costs in some scenarios. 
2) For the buyout multiple, could we do 2 months of committed fees (instead of 3) but allow Olivetech to claim a partial pro-rated refund if the incident sequence continues after the buyout window? In short: smaller immediate buyout, with a safety-net if problems persist.

If Redwood can accept those two tweaks, we'll circulate to Olivetech Legal and aim to return redlines by Dec 9. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if helpful.

—Emma
